deep.reconstruction:
The page is a printed textbook page, p. 20 of a German elementary arithmetic and algebra text (the bundle name suggests Leiste). It is interleaved, and Gauss wrote only a column of short labels in the right margin. The derivations are all in the print, plus the matching notes on the facing page.

Printed text:
(end of §46) Like powers, i.e. same base and same exponent, combine by adding coefficients:
- 2a^2 + 3a^2 = 5a^2
- 3ab - ab = 2ab
- 6a^2b^3 - 4a^2b^3 = 2a^2b^3
- 5a^2 ± 4a^3 cannot be simplified.

§47 (theorem): multiplying powers of the same base means adding exponents (logarithms).
- a^3·a^2 = a^5, and in general a^m a^n = a^{m+n}.
- Hence log_a(a^m a^n) = m + n.
- Example 16·64 = 1024: base 4 gives 2+3 = 5 = log_4 1024; base 2 gives 4+6 = 10 = log_2 1024.

§48 (relating two log systems): put c = a^m, so c^n = a^{nm}.
- With c = 4, a = 2, m = 2: 4^5 = 2^10 = 1024.
- Implicitly (my gloss) log_a x = m·log_c x.

§49 (theorem): dividing powers of the same base means subtracting exponents, a^m/a^n = a^{m-n}.
- Example a^6/a^4 = a^2; with a = 3, 729/81 = 9.
- log_3 729 - log_3 81 = 6 - 4 = 2 = log_3 9.

Gauss's margin:
- Labels: 'chorda / arcus / sin', 0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, 90°, dsin, dcos, Sin, cos, 1/sin, 1/cos, φ, m(?), s/c, dt.
- These are the row headings of his work on the facing (next) page, on the lemniscatic sine.
- There the half-period ϖ/2 is divided into '90°', and he lists:
  - s(45°) = sl(ϖ/4) = sqrt(sqrt2 - 1) ≈ 0.6435943.
  - s(60°) = sl(ϖ/3) = (sqrt12 - 3)^{1/4} ≈ 0.8253788.
  - s(30°) = sl(ϖ/6) = cl(ϖ/3) = sqrt((1-σ)/(1+σ)) with σ = sqrt(sqrt12 - 3). This equals (1-σ)/sqrt(4 - sqrt12) ≈ 0.43542.
- He also gives derivative formulas, and series for sl, cl, 1/sl, 1/cl and for the inverse φ = ∫ds/sqrt(1-s^4).
- He introduces t = s/c by analogy with the tangent.
- On this page itself Gauss makes only the label list; no computation.
errors: No errors in the printed mathematics on this page.

On the next page, '(sqrt12-3)^{1/4} = sqrt(sqrt(3/2) - sqrt(1/2))' is false as written (0.8254 vs 0.7194). Gauss's adjacent marginal factor 3^{1/8} corrects it: (2sqrt3 - 3)^{1/4} = 3^{1/8}·sqrt(sqrt(3/2) - sqrt(1/2)). The bare equality is a transcription or reading artifact, or an unfinished step, not this page's error.
